title: Lease supervisor and service-slicing for graceful tenant degradation in private control planes
creator: Marcus Liu
description: Problem: Private/VPC control planes need a deterministic, low-risk way to isolate overloaded tenants and perform upgrades without broad availability impacts. Existing strategies (broad throttles, region-level quarantines) are effective but coarse and lead to noisy failure modes for mid-critical tenants. Goal: implement a lease-supervisor pattern combined with service-slicing to provide per-tenant admission control, timeboxed degradation windows, and multi-region lease handoff so tenants can be evicted or degraded gracefully with observable SLO impact and safe rollback semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant lease state machine implemented in control plane with TTL and renewal semantics
Service-slicing hooks added to serving runtime so requests can be routed to 'degraded' slice with reduced concurrency and quantization profiles
Circuit-breaker policy that triggers lease downgrade or eviction when tenant-specific latency/error SLOs exceed threshold
Multi-region lease handoff documented and exercised in chaos tests (primary -> standby region takeover) without orphaned leases
Rollback path: automated lease release and rapid reintegration without cross-tenant disruption
Runbook and alerting created for on-call when lease supervisor escalates tenant degradations
technical_notes: Lease Supervisor: lightweight, etcd-backed leaderless coordinator per control-plane with per-tenant lease object (state: Normal, Degraded, Evicted, Draining)
Lease TTL = 60s by default; renewals use heartbeat from tenant proxy; supervisor enforces backoff windows to avoid flip-flopping
Service Slices: runtime will expose slices: normal, degraded-1 (lower concurrency), degraded-2 (read-only or smaller context-window), offline
Admission Controller: consults lease state and enforces per-tenant qps/concurrency limits and routing to slices
Circuit Breaker Triggers: rolling 1m P95 latency breach OR error-rate increase + token bucket exhaustion
Compatibility: must interoperate with Dedicated autoscaling and existing fallback routing to cheaper model variant
Security: lease state must be access-controlled; API endpoints require tenant-scoped RBAC tokens
implementation_plan: Week 1: design doc and state machine definition; API schema for lease objects; review with SRE and product
Week 2: implement lease supervisor prototype (etcd-backed) and local emulator for dev; add unit tests
Week 3: add admission controller hooks to private control plane; stub runtime slice routing and fallback paths
Week 4: integrate circuit-breaker signals (latency/error metrics) into supervisor decisions; add metrics and tracing
Week 5: end-to-end QA in staging, implement multi-region handoff logic and conservative defaults
Week 6: run chaos experiments (network partition, simulate tenant spike) and iterate on TTL/backoff
Week 7: create runbook, on-call playbook, and rollout to a small cohort of customers
Week 8: monitor, collect SLO regressions, and expand rollout
rollout_plan: Canary: enable lease-supervisor in 1 private customer region with monitoring and an opt-in flag
Cohort 1: 5 customers (non-critical) for 2 weeks; gather telemetry; reduce aggressiveness if false positives
Cohort 2: expand to 25 customers with varied workload shapes; run automated rollback tests weekly
Full: flip default to enabled for all private control planes after 8 weeks and stable metrics
Fallback: operator can set global 'lease-mode=permissive' to disable eviction logic while leaving observability on
test_plan: Unit tests for lease lifecycle transitions (renew, degrade, evict, drain, reinstate)
Integration test for admission controller refusal + runtime routing to degraded slice
E2E test: simulate tenant spike and verify that only the target tenant's requests are limited and other tenants maintain SLOs
Multi-region handoff test: partition primary region and ensure standby picks up leases within SLA
Load test: verify degraded slices reduce P95 latency for other tenants under heavy load
Security test: verify RBAC prevents unauthorized lease manipulation
risks: False positives: overly aggressive eviction could impact healthy tenants if metrics noisy
Lease split-brain on network partitions leading to double-eviction or stuck evicted state
Integration with existing autoscaler and rollback semantics may have race conditions
Customer confusion: tenants may not understand degraded behavior without clear telemetry in Console
Operational complexity: more state in control plane increases debugging surface for on-call
